Scope, prerequisites, and privacy

Checks data variables, lifecycle IDs, product-reference syntax, internal links, fragments, and media paths. No external website requests. A batch resolves the chosen folders and articles at launch and checks only that fixed article set in one host task.

Product availability, prose accuracy, external links, rendered media, navigation, and generated content are not verified. Product references can remain unverified because no product manifest is supplied.

Requires installed Node.js and checker dependencies, a trusted checkout, and a Copilot host with background-task APIs. The host can require permissions. It owns execution; this canvas does not sandbox agents, create worktrees, schedule runs, install tools, or interpret article text as instructions.

Saved findings appear while current freshness is checked in a local worker. Checking is not Fresh. Complete, confirmed reports enter the inbox only after full validation. Every decision save freshly validates the selected article and its dependencies. Changed evidence reopens decisions. Findings absent from a later applicable scan remain marked Not observed, never automatically fixed. Failed or incomplete attempts preserve earlier results.

Recent host activity is not saved as a transcript. Hidden execution references support provenance and recovery, not run-history navigation. The task API returns no host deep links. Stopping local freshness verification never cancels a host task. Local review never authorizes documentation edits, GitHub writes, media approval, publication, host-task cancellation, or archiving.

PR review, feature documentation, audits, media, replay, and docs-as-eval remain separate workflows.
